mainTopic: Whether a worker eats משלו or משל שמים, the eating rights of watchmen (רב vs. שמואל), and the four kinds of guards.
overview: The amud begins by testing explanations of a contradiction. The משנה says a man may not stipulate away the eating rights of his minor slaves, but רבי הושעיא's ברייתא lets him do it for his Canaanite slaves, young or grown. After several answers are rejected, the גמרא concludes that the two sources disagree about whether a worker eats משלו (as part of his earnings) or משל שמים (as a Torah gift). Next comes the full משנה: who can trade away the right to eat, workers handling נטע רבעי or untithed produce, and watchmen who eat only by local custom. רב and שמואל argue over which watchmen that rule covers. The argument turns on whether guarding counts as work. שמואל's view survives two challenges, from the guard of the פרה אדומה and from the guard of cucumber fields, and רב אשי proves it from the wording of an earlier משנה. A new משנה then lists the four kinds of guards and their duties to swear or pay. The גמרא shows it follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a renter has the law of a paid guard: four guards, but three sets of laws. The amud ends with a story of a shepherd whose animal slipped into the river, whom רבה exempted.

steps.title: The earlier answer only works for one view about feeding slaves
steps.stepSummary: The earlier answer (it depends on whether the master feeds them) works if a master must feed his slave. It fails if a master is allowed to say 'work for me and I won't feed you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for the one who says a master cannot say to his slave, 'Work for me and I won't feed you.' But for the one who says the master can say that, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its earlier answer. That answer only makes sense according to one opinion about whether a master must feed his slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a master must feed his slave, then he cannot take away the slave's eating rights while working, so the משנה's rule makes sense. But if a master may refuse to feed his slave entirely, he should surely be able to cancel the slave's right to eat while working. So the earlier distinction doesn't hold up for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this view, but not for another)
Work for me and I will not feed you
What can be said? (signals a difficulty)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
a master cannot say to a slave
'Work with me and I will not feed you' — it is fine.
phrases.notes: 'It is fine' means the earlier answer works well for this opinion.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
a master can say to a slave
'Work with me and I will not feed you,'
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the earlier answer (from before this section) that the משנה and ברייתא differ on whether the master feeds them.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier distinction between a master who feeds and one who does not feed his slaves
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a master may refuse to feed a slave altogether, he should be able to cancel the slave's eating while working. So the משנה's ban cannot be explained by that distinction.

steps.title: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about feeding slaves
steps.stepSummary: New answer: both sources speak of a master who does not feed his slaves, and they argue about whether he is allowed to refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both speak of a case where he does not give them food, and this is what they argue about: one Sage holds he can, and one Sage holds he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new answer. The משנה and the ברייתא are simply arguing about whether a master may say 'work for me and I won't feed you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of putting the two sources in different cases, the גמרא now has them argue about the same case. The ברייתא holds the master can refuse food, so he can also cancel eating while working. The משנה holds he cannot refuse, so he cannot cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.english: Rather, both this and that
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the משנה and רבי הושעיא's ברייתא.

phrases.english: are where he does not provide them with food,
and they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds he can,
and one Sage holds he cannot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּשֶׁאֵין מַעֲלֶה לָהֶן מְזוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by turning the two sources into a disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the contradiction into a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources speak of different cases (feeding vs. not feeding).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both speak of not feeding; they argue about whether a master may refuse to feed his slave.

steps.title: Would רבי יוחנן really ignore the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: Problem: רבי יוחנן rules that a master can refuse to feed his slave. Under the new answer, he would be siding with a ברייתא against a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, who says the master can, leaves the משנה and follows the ברייתא?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 2. If that answer were right, רבי יוחנן would be ruling like the ברייתא and against the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן is known to rule that a master may say 'I won't feed you.' Under step 2, that is the ברייתא's view, and the משנה disagrees. It is hard to believe רבי יוחנן would abandon a משנה for a ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: The question mark is a challenge. The גמרא is not saying רבי יוחנן actually ignored the משנה; it is saying he surely would not, so the answer of step 2 must be wrong.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן, who says: the master can,
phrases.notes: He means the master can say to his slave, 'Work for me and I won't feed you.'

phrases.english: leaves aside the משנה
and acts according to the ברייתא?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר: יָכוֹל הָרַב, שָׁבֵיק מַתְנִיתִין וְעָבֵיד כְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 2's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 2's claim that the משנה holds a master cannot refuse to feed his slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן rules that the master can. Under step 2 he would be ruling against a משנה in favor of a ברייתא, which is unlikely.

steps.title: Both agree he eats from Heaven; 'stipulate' means feeding beforehand
steps.stepSummary: New answer: everyone agrees the worker eats 'from Heaven,' so no one can cancel his eating. רבי הושעיא's 'stipulate' means arranging food in advance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees he eats from Heaven's, and he cannot stipulate it away. And what is the 'stipulates' that רבי הושעיא said? Food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third answer. There is no real argument, and the word 'stipulate' in the ברייתא means something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worker's food is a gift from the Torah (משל שמים), the father or master has no right to cancel it, and that is the משנה's point. רבי הושעיא's 'קוצץ' means the master feeds them before work so they won't want to eat during work. That is a different act, so the sources no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He eats from Heaven's property; his food is a Torah gift, not part of his wages
Stipulates; makes an arrangement in advance

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
he eats from what belongs to Heaven,
and he cannot stipulate.
And what is the 'stipulates' that רבי הושעיא said?
Food.
phrases.notes: He means he arranges to feed them before work, so they won't be hungry to eat during it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִשֶּׁל שָׁמַיִם הוּא אוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 2 with a new reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets a word in the ברייתא so there is no dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קוצץ' in the ברייתא means cancelling the eating rights, which would contradict the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees the eating cannot be cancelled. 'קוצץ' means giving food beforehand.

steps.title: Then he could do the same for his animal
steps.stepSummary: Problem: if 'stipulate' just means feeding beforehand, he could do that with straw for his animal too. Yet רבי הושעיא's ברייתא says one cannot stipulate for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, regarding his animal, let him stipulate straw for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 4. Under that reading, the ברייתא's exclusion of the animal makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding beforehand is allowed for anyone, including an animal: just give it straw before work. But רבי הושעיא's ברייתא says one cannot stipulate for his animal. So 'stipulate' must mean something more than feeding in advance.

phrases.english: Similarly, regarding his animal,
let him stipulate straw for it!
phrases.notes: Meaning: feed it straw before work, which is obviously allowed. So why does the משנה say he can't stipulate for an animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְווֹתֵיהּ גַּבֵּי בְּהֶמְתּוֹ תֶּבֶן נִקּוֹץ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 4's reading of 'קוצץ'.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's explanation that 'קוצץ' means feeding beforehand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Feeding beforehand works equally for an animal. Yet the משנה rules out stipulating for an animal, so that cannot be what 'קוצץ' means.

steps.title: Final answer: they disagree whether he eats 'from his own' or 'from Heaven'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה and ברייתא disagree about whether a worker's eating is part of his own wages (משלו) or a gift from Heaven (משל שמים).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they disagree about: one Sage holds he eats from his own, and one Sage holds he eats from Heaven's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The משנה and the ברייתא are arguing about the nature of the worker's right to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the explanation followed here, the משנה's תנא holds the worker eats משלו, as part of what he earns. The ברייתא's תנא holds he eats משל שמים. This difference explains why they rule differently about stipulating for minors and slaves, and it shows the משלו / משל שמים question is an argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: He eats from his own; his food counts as part of his earnings

steps.whatToRemember: After three answers were rejected, the גמרא concludes that the משנה and רבי הושעיא's ברייתא disagree about whether a worker eats משלו or משל שמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question whether a worker eats משלו or משל שמים was asked earlier in the sugya. This shows it is already an argument between תנאים.

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds he eats from his own,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר – מִשֶּׁל שָׁמַיִם הוּא אוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: and one Sage holds he eats from Heaven's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 4 with a new dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Turns the contradiction into a dispute between תנאים on a basic question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees he eats משל שמים, and 'קוצץ' means feeding beforehand.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue whether the worker eats משלו or משל שמים.

steps.title: Who can trade away the right to eat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person can give up the right to eat, for himself or for adult family members and slaves who understand. He cannot do it for minors or for his animal, who lack understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: A man can agree to take extra pay instead of eating. He can make this deal for himself, for his adult son and daughter, for his adult slave and maidservant, and for his wife, because they have understanding. But he cannot make it for his minor son and daughter, his minor slave and maidservant, or his animal, because they do not have understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists who can have their right to eat traded away for a fixed sum. Adults with understanding can agree to it. Minors and animals cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up a right only works when the person can agree to it. So the line is drawn by דעת, mature understanding. Notice that the animal is placed with those who cannot give up their eating; this is the משנה whose view the earlier steps contrasted with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'cuts'; sets a fixed payment in place of the right to eat
Mature understanding; the ability to agree to something
Minors, who are not yet legally adults

steps.confusionAlert: The master is not taking away their food by force. The deal only works for people who can agree to give up their own right, and that is why minors and animals are left out.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ קוֹצֵץ אָדָם עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: MISHNA: A man may stipulate on his own behalf
phrases.notes: 'Stipulate' here means he agrees to get a set amount of extra pay instead of eating the fruit he works with.

phrases.english: on behalf of his adult son and daughter,
on behalf of his adult slave and maidservant,
on behalf of his wife,
because they have understanding.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵינוֹ קוֹצֵץ עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים,
phrases.english: But he may not stipulate on behalf of his minor son and daughter,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים,
phrases.english: nor on behalf of his minor slave and maidservant,
nor on behalf of his animal,
because they do not have understanding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the full משנה text whose animal ruling the earlier steps compared with the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who has דעת can give up the right to eat for a fixed sum. Minors and animals cannot, so no one can make this deal for them.

steps.title: Workers with fourth-year fruit or untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: Workers handling נטע רבעי, or produce whose work is already finished, may not eat it. But if the owner did not tell them, he must redeem or tithe the produce and feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who hires workers to work with his fourth-year fruit: these workers may not eat. If he did not tell them, he must redeem the fruit and feed them. If his fig cakes broke apart or his wine barrels opened, these workers may not eat. If he did not tell them, he must tithe the food and feed them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases where workers normally may not eat, because the produce is not yet allowed to be eaten freely. It adds that if the owner kept quiet, he must fix the problem and feed them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נטע רבעי cannot be eaten casually before it is redeemed. Fig cakes and wine whose work is already done are now obligated in מעשר, and a worker does not eat from produce at that stage. If the workers were not warned, they took the job expecting to eat, so the owner must redeem or tithe the food for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's fourth year, which must be redeemed or eaten in ירושלים
Redeems; moves the fruit's holiness onto money
His round cakes of pressed figs

phrases.english: One who hires workers
to work with his fourth-year fruit,
phrases.notes: Fourth-year fruit is holy. It must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed first, so workers can't just snack on it.

phrases.english: these workers may not eat.
If he did not inform them, he must redeem it and feed them.
If his fig cakes broke apart,
or his barrels came open,
these workers may not eat.
If he did not inform them, he must tithe it and feed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֲלִים לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּנֶטַע רְבָעִי שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with cases where the right to eat is blocked by the produce's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers may not eat produce that is forbidden until redeemed or tithed. If they were not told beforehand, the owner must make the food permitted and feed them.

steps.title: Watchmen of produce eat by local custom
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that watchmen who guard produce may eat from it only because of local custom, not by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Watchmen of produce eat according to the local custom, but not by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a rule about people who only guard produce. They may eat, but only because local practice allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's right to eat belongs to someone who works with the produce. A watchman just guards it, so the משנה says his eating comes from custom and not from the Torah. This sets up the גמרא's discussion right after.

keyTerms.meaning: The custom or practice of the place

phrases.english: Watchmen of produce may eat
by local custom,
but not by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the משנה, turning from workers to watchmen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A watchman's eating is allowed by local custom only, not by Torah law.

steps.title: רב limits the watchman rule to growing produce
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's rule (custom only) applies to watchmen of gardens and orchards. Watchmen of winepresses and piles of harvested produce eat by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The משנה said 'watchmen of produce.' רב said: They taught this only about watchmen of gardens and orchards. But watchmen of winepresses and grain piles eat by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting the משנה's words 'watchmen of produce.' רב then narrows them: the 'custom only' rule covers just watchmen of produce that is still growing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounded like it covered every watchman. רב splits it in two. For produce still attached to the ground (gardens, orchards), the watchman eats by custom only. For harvested produce (winepresses, piles), the watchman has a real Torah right to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this about…; a formula that limits a rule
Gardens and orchards, where produce is still growing

phrases.english: GEMARA: "Watchmen of produce."
Rav said: They taught this only
about watchmen of gardens and orchards.
But watchmen of winepresses and piles
eat by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שׁוֹמְרֵי גַנּוֹת וּפַרְדֵּסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה's watchman rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watchmen of growing produce eat by custom. Watchmen of harvested produce eat by Torah law.

steps.title: רב's reasoning: guarding counts as work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב must hold that a person who guards produce is treated like someone who does work on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that one who guards is considered like one who does work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out what idea lies behind רב's statement: in his view, guarding counts as a kind of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a worker has a Torah right to eat. Since רב gives watchmen of harvested produce that Torah right, he must see guarding as work. This makes the watchman a true worker in the Torah's eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; introduces the reasoning behind someone's view
Is considered like one who does work

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, guarding counts as work. So a watchman of harvested produce eats by Torah law, while a watchman of growing produce eats only by local custom.

phrases.english: He holds: one who guards is considered like one who does work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the principle behind רב's limit on the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב holds that guarding is treated as doing work, which gives a watchman a worker's Torah right to eat.

steps.title: שמואל: Only watchmen of harvested produce eat, and only by custom
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה's custom-based eating applies only to watchmen of winepresses and piles. Watchmen of gardens and orchards may not eat at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The משנה's rule was taught only about watchmen of winepresses and piles. But watchmen of gardens and orchards do not eat, not by Torah law and not by local custom.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second reading of the משנה about watchmen, and it is the reverse of רב's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the משנה's 'custom only' rule is about gardens and orchards, and watchmen of harvested produce eat by Torah law. For שמואל, the 'custom only' rule is about harvested produce, and watchmen of gardens and orchards get nothing at all. So for שמואל, no watchman ever eats by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Piles of harvested grain or produce

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch. רב and שמואל list the SAME two kinds of watchmen, but they reverse which kind gets which rule.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
They taught [this] only
about watchmen of winepresses and piles.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's rule that watchmen eat by local custom.

phrases.english: But watchmen of gardens and orchards
do not eat
not by Torah law
and not by local custom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the משנה from רב's reading in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watchmen of winepresses and piles eat only by custom. Watchmen of gardens and orchards may not eat at all.

steps.title: שמואל holds that a guard is not like a worker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל must hold that guarding produce is not the same as working on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that one who guards is not considered like one who does work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the idea behind שמואל's ruling. This sets up the two challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact opposite of what step 11 said about רב. Since a guard is not a worker, the Torah's permission for workers to eat never covers him. Any eating he does can only come from custom.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not considered like one who does work

steps.whatToRemember: רב says a guard counts as a worker. שמואל says a guard does not count as a worker. The rest of the sugya tests שמואל's view.

phrases.english: He holds that one who guards
is not considered like one who does work.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר מְשַׁמֵּר לָאו כְּעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind שמואל's ruling in step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For שמואל, guarding does not count as working.

steps.title: Challenge: The guard of the פרה אדומה becomes טמא
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הונא cites a teaching that a person who guards the פרה אדומה makes his clothes טמא. That implies a guard counts as a participant in the work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב הונא raised an objection: One who guards the פרה makes his clothes טמא. If you say a guard is not considered like one who does work, why does he make his clothes טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר רב הונא challenges שמואל's idea that a guard is not a worker. He uses a case from the laws of the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those who do the work of the פרה אדומה become טמא. If even the person who only guards it becomes טמא, guarding seems to count as doing the work. That goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer, whose ashes are used for purification

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna raised an objection:
One who guards the heifer
phrases.notes: This is the פרה אדומה, the red heifer. במדבר 19

phrases.english: makes [his] clothes impure.
And if you say that one who guards
is not considered like one who does work,
why does he make [his] clothes impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's idea that a guard is not like a worker
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The guard of the פרה becomes טמא just like the people who work on it, so guarding seems to count as work.

steps.title: Answer: It is a rabbinic precaution in case he moves a limb
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא answers that the guard becomes טמא only by a rabbinic decree. Since the guard might move a part of the פרה, the rabbis made all guards טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: It is a decree, in case he moves a limb of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא defends שמואל. He explains that the guard's טומאה does not come from guarding itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the פרה is real work. The rabbis worried that a guard might move one of its limbs, so they made every guard טמא as a safeguard. Guarding by itself still does not count as work.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
[It is] a decree, in case he moves a limb of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the source of the rule to a rabbinic safeguard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The guard becomes טמא because guarding counts as work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guard becomes טמא only by rabbinic decree, in case he moves part of the פרה. Guarding itself is not work.

steps.title: Challenge: The guard of cucumber fields may eat
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא cites a teaching that a guard of several cucumber fields eats a proportional amount from each field. If a guard is not a worker, why may he eat at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא raised an objection: One who guards four or five cucumber fields should not fill his stomach from one of them. Rather, he eats from each one according to its share. If you say a guard is not considered like one who does work, why does he eat?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a second challenge to שמואל. He uses a case where a guard of growing fields is allowed to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching assumes the guard has a right to eat. It only limits how he divides his eating between the fields. Cucumber fields are like gardens, and שמואל said guards of gardens may not eat at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He should not fill his stomach
In proportion, by its fair share

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
One who guards four or five cucumber fields
should not fill his stomach
from one of them,
rather, from each and every one
he eats according to [its] share.
And if you say that one who guards
is not considered like one who does work,
why does he eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to שמואל's reasoning, after the first was answered in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that a guard is not a worker and that guards of growing produce do not eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source lets a guard of growing fields eat, which suggests a guard counts as a worker.

steps.title: Answer: The teaching is about picked cucumbers
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי answers that the teaching is about cucumbers that were already picked. Watching harvested produce lets a guard eat by custom, and שמואל agrees to that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: They taught this about picked cucumbers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי defends שמואל. He says the cucumber teaching is about produce that has already been picked off the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allows watchmen of harvested produce, like piles, to eat by local custom. If the cucumbers were already picked, the guard is eating by custom, not by Torah law. So the teaching fits with שמואל.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
They taught [this] about uprooted [cucumbers].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: בַּעֲקוּרִין שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching is about cucumbers still growing in the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about picked cucumbers, where the guard eats by custom, as שמואל allows.

steps.title: Challenge: Picked cucumbers are already finished
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: once cucumbers are picked, isn't their work already finished for מעשר? If so, no one should be allowed to eat them while working.
steps.simpleTranslation: Picked? But isn't their work already finished with regard to מעשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב שימי בר אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 taught that workers may not eat produce whose work is already finished. If picked cucumbers are finished for מעשר, then even custom should not let the guard eat them, so the answer seems not to work.

phrases.english: Uprooted?
But isn't their work finished with regard to tithes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's claim that the cucumbers were picked
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Picked cucumbers are finished for מעשר, and produce whose work is finished may not be eaten by workers.

steps.title: Answer: Their blossom was not yet removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cucumbers were picked but still had their blossom on them. So their work was not yet finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where their blossom was not removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and finishes defending שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing the blossom is still part of the work on cucumbers. As long as the blossom is on, the work is not finished for מעשר. So the guard of picked cucumbers may still eat by custom, and the teaching fits שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The blossom or fuzz at the tip of a cucumber

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל holds that a guard is not a worker. Both challenges were answered. The guard of the פרה is טמא only by rabbinic decree. The cucumber guard eats by custom, because the cucumbers were picked but still unfinished.

phrases.english: [It is] where their blossom was not removed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Picked cucumbers are finished for מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Picked cucumbers whose blossom is still on are not yet finished, so the guard may eat by custom.

steps.title: רב אשי brings support for שמואל from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says שמואל's view makes sense. The משנה says 'these eat מן התורה', which implies that someone else eats only by local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It makes sense to follow שמואל. We learned in a משנה: 'These workers eat מן התורה: one who works with produce still attached to the ground when its work is being finished, and one who works with detached produce, etc.' That wording implies there is someone who does not eat מן התורה, but only because of local custom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a proof for שמואל's view that a guard eats only because of local custom, not מן התורה. He points to the exact wording of an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not just say 'these workers eat.' It said 'these eat מן התורה.' That extra phrase hints that there is another group who eats for a different reason, local custom. This fits שמואל, who said a guard of picked produce eats by custom.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is logical
Still attached to the ground (not yet picked)
The finishing stage of the produce's work, such as harvesting
Local custom; the accepted practice of the place
By implication; it follows from the wording

steps.confusionAlert: 'Eating by local custom' is still a real permission to eat. It is just not a Torah-level right. Don't mix up 'not מן התורה' with 'not allowed at all.'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It makes sense to follow Shmuel's view,
as we learned in a Mishnah: And these workers eat by Torah law:
one who works with produce attached to the ground
at the time its work is being finished,
and one who works with detached produce, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the משנה goes on. The full line says this applies before the detached produce's work is finished.

phrases.english: This implies that there is someone
who does not eat by Torah law
but only by local custom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 18-19 defended שמואל's reading, רב אשי now brings positive support for שמואל from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a guard of picked produce eats by local custom, not מן התורה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'ואלו אוכלין מן התורה' (on 87a), which implies another group eats only by custom.

steps.title: The end of the משנה shows who cannot eat at all
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says 'these do not eat.' That cannot mean 'not מן התורה but by custom,' because the first part already taught that. So it means they do not eat at all. This includes workers with unfinished attached produce, and even more so guards of gardens and orchards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: 'And these do not eat.' What does 'do not eat' mean? If you say it means they don't eat מן התורה but do eat by local custom, that is the same thing the first part already taught. So it must mean they don't eat at all, neither מן התורה nor by local custom. Who are they? One who works with attached produce when its work is not being finished, and all the more so guards of gardens and orchards.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי keeps building his proof by reading the second half of the same משנה. He shows that 'do not eat' must mean 'not at all.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half already hinted at a group that eats by custom. So the second half must describe people who get nothing at all, and it includes 'all the more so guards of gardens and orchards.' That is the key point against רב, who said guards of gardens and orchards do eat by custom, and it matches שמואל exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or teaching
The first part of a משנה or teaching
That is the same as; nothing new

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels: workers who eat מן התורה, guards of picked produce who eat by local custom (שמואל), and guards of attached produce who do not eat at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the long discussion about whether a guard counts as a worker who may eat. The answer depends on whether the produce is already picked.

phrases.english: Say the end part of the Mishnah:
And these are the ones who do not eat.
What does 'do not eat' mean?
If you say it means they do not eat by Torah law
but do eat by local custom, that is the same as the first part,
phrases.notes: The first part, from step 20, already hinted at a group that eats only by custom. So this would just repeat it.

phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean they do not eat

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִן הַתּוֹרָה וְלֹא מֵהִלְכוֹת מְדִינָה.
phrases.english: neither by Torah law nor by local custom?
And who are they?
One who works with produce attached to the ground
at a time when its work is not being finished,
and all the more so guards of gardens and orchards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's proof by reading the second half of the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's three-level picture: some eat מן התורה, some by custom, some not at all.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא 'ואלו שאינן אוכלין', which must mean 'not at all,' or else it would repeat the רישא.

steps.title: New משנה: the four kinds of guards
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four kinds of guards: שומר חנם, שואל, נושא שכר, and שוכר. A שומר חנם swears in every case, and a שואל pays in every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are four kinds of guards: an unpaid guard, a borrower, a paid guard, and a renter. An unpaid guard swears an oath about everything, and a borrower pays for everything.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and names the four kinds of people who hold someone else's property. It then gives the rule for the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more the guard benefits, the more responsibility he carries. A שומר חנם gets nothing, so he only swears that the loss happened as he says, and then he is free. A שואל gets all the benefit, so he pays no matter what happened.

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid guard who watches an item for free
A borrower who uses an item for free
A renter who pays to use an item

steps.confusionAlert: 'The borrower pays for everything' means even for things outside his control, like the animal dying on its own. That is much stricter than the other three guards.

phrases.english: Mishnah: There are four kinds of guards:
an unpaid guard and the borrower,
a paid guard and the renter.
An unpaid guard swears an oath about everything,
phrases.notes: He swears that it really happened as he says, and then he does not have to pay.

phrases.english: and the borrower pays for everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The discussion of workers eating is over, and a new משנה about guards' responsibility begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four kinds of guards. A שומר חנם swears in every case, and a שואל pays in every case.

steps.title: The paid guard and the renter: swear for some cases, pay for others
steps.stepSummary: A נושא שכר and a שוכר swear when the animal was injured, captured, or died. They must pay when it was lost or stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A paid guard and a renter swear an oath if the animal was injured, captured, or died. But they pay if it was lost or stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by giving the rule for the two middle guards, the paid guard and the renter. They have the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two are in the middle, so their rule is in the middle. For injury, capture, or death, which are outside their control, they swear and are free. For loss or theft, which a careful guard should prevent, they must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was injured (literally, broken)
An animal that was captured, for example by raiders

steps.whatToRemember: There is a ladder of responsibility. A שומר חנם swears for everything. A נושא שכר or שוכר swears for accidents but pays for loss or theft. A שואל pays for everything.
steps.whyThisMatters: These four categories are the basic framework for the whole topic of guarding other people's property, which the next chapter discusses at length.

phrases.english: And a paid guard and a renter
swear an oath about an injured animal,
about a captured animal, and about a dead animal,
but they pay for something lost or stolen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, giving the rule for the remaining two guards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נושא שכר and a שוכר swear for injury, capture, or death, and pay for loss or theft.

steps.title: Who taught the four guards?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא is the author of the משנה about four kinds of guards.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who taught 'four guards'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking whose opinion it follows. This question sets up the whole discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often asks 'מאן תנא' when a משנה seems to take a side in a debate. Here the question is about the משנה's list of four guards and the rules it gives them.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (author) of this teaching?
Four kinds of guards: unpaid, borrower, paid, and renter
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
Who is the tanna who taught 'four guards'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of the four guards quoted in steps 22-23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה of the four guards follows.

steps.title: It is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: It is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the answer: the משנה is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is short and does not yet explain which detail of the משנה belongs to רבי מאיר. That missing detail is exactly what the next step attacks.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
It is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.

steps.title: Doesn't everyone agree there are four guards?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: is there anyone who does not hold of four guards? Why tie it to רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Is there anyone who does not hold of four guards?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the answer. Everyone agrees the תורה speaks of four kinds of guards, so naming רבי מאיר seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of four guards comes from the פסוקים and is accepted by all. So if רב נחמן meant the number four, there would be no reason to name one תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Who does not hold of it

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אַרְבָּעָה שׁוֹמְרִין?
phrases.english: Is there anyone who does not hold of four guards?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that the משנה of four guards is רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All agree there are four guards, so the number four cannot be what makes this רבי מאיר's view.

steps.title: The point is that a renter is like a paid guard
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: he meant that the view that a שוכר is like a נושא שכר is רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I am telling you: Who taught that a renter is like a paid guard? It is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן clarifies what he really meant. The special detail is that the משנה gives the שוכר the same rules as the נושא שכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the משנה put the נושא שכר and the שוכר together with the same law. That ruling is debated, and רב נחמן says it follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I meant to tell you
A renter, who pays to use the item

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I am saying to you:
Who is the tanna who holds a renter is like a paid guard?
It is Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by narrowing what רב נחמן meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן seemed to say only רבי מאיר holds of four guards.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant only רבי מאיר holds that a שוכר has the law of a נושא שכר.

steps.title: A ברייתא says רבי מאיר holds the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a שומר חנם, and רבי יהודה says like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard רבי מאיר say the opposite! As it is taught: A renter, how does he pay? רבי מאיר says: like an unpaid guard. רבי יהודה says: like a paid guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא. There, רבי מאיר compares the שוכר to a שומר חנם, not to a paid guard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a שומר חנם, then the משנה, which makes him like a נושא שכר, should be רבי יהודה. This directly contradicts רב נחמן.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But we heard Rabbi Meir say the opposite,
as it is taught: A renter, how does he pay?
Rabbi Meir says: Like an unpaid guard;
Rabbi Yehuda says: Like a paid guard!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the clarified answer of step 27 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי מאיר holds a שוכר is like a נושא שכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר saying a שוכר is like a שומר חנם, the opposite.

steps.title: רבה בר אבוה reverses the names
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה learns the ברייתא with the opinions switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר אבוה teaches it the opposite way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה בר אבוה had a version of the ברייתא with the names flipped. In his version, רבי מאיר says a שוכר is like a paid guard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction: it depends on how the ברייתא is learned. By רבה בר אבוה's version, the משנה fits רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: He teaches it the opposite way

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר changed his mind. The point is that רבה בר אבוה had a different version of the ברייתא with the two names switched.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Avuh teaches it the opposite way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the source (switching the names)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows רבי מאיר compares a שוכר to a שומר חנם.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רבה בר אבוה's version, רבי מאיר compares a שוכר to a שומר שכר, matching the משנה.

steps.title: Then there are only three guards
steps.stepSummary: If a שוכר is the same as a נושא שכר, why does the משנה say four guards? There are only three.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, four? They are three!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new problem. If the renter and paid guard have the same rules, the count of four seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the שוכר is just like the נושא שכר, there seem to be only three distinct guards. So why would the משנה count four?

phrases.english: If so, four?
They are three!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that a שוכר is like a נושא שכר and attacks the משנה's number.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two of the guards share one law, there are really only three.

steps.title: Four guards, three sets of laws
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says there are four kinds of guards, but only three sets of laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Four guards, and their laws are three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה counts four kinds of people, even though two of them share one set of rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number four counts the types of guards, not the number of different laws. The שוכר is still its own type, even though its outcome matches the נושא שכר.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה of the four guards follows רבי מאיר (as רבה בר אבוה learned the ברייתא): a שוכר has the law of a נושא שכר. There are four kinds of guards but only three sets of laws.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Four guards, and their laws are three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 and closes the discussion about who taught the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Four' means four different sets of laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Four' counts the kinds of guards; their laws are only three.

steps.title: The shepherd whose animal fell into the river
steps.stepSummary: A shepherd's animal slipped into the נהר פפא. He came to רבה, who exempted him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a shepherd herding animals on the bank of the נהר פפא. One of them slipped and fell into the water. He came before רבה, and רבה exempted him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a story. A shepherd lost an animal in the river, and רבה ruled he does not have to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shepherd is paid, so he is a נושא שכר. A paid guard pays for theft and loss, but not for an accident he could not prevent, so the question is which kind of case this was.

phrases.english: There was a certain shepherd
who was herding animals
on the bank of the Pappa River.
One of them slipped and fell into the water.
He came before Rabba, and he exempted him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא רָעֲיָא דַּהֲוָה קָא רָעֵי חֵיוָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: a practical case about a paid guard's liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה exempted a shepherd whose animal slipped into the river.

steps.title: רבה's reason: what could he have done?
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains his ruling: the shepherd could not have done anything to prevent it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: What could he have done?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the reason for exempting the shepherd. The fall was something the shepherd could not stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה treats the drowning as an accident beyond the shepherd's control, a case where even a paid guard is exempt. This reasoning sets up what the גמרא will discuss next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line shows the key test for a paid guard: if he truly could not prevent the loss, he does not pay.

phrases.english: He said: What could he have done?
phrases.notes: He means the shepherd had no way to stop the animal from slipping, so it was not his fault.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבה's ruling in step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A paid guard is exempt when the loss was beyond his control and he could have done nothing to prevent it.
